subject: biology
title: The immune system and white blood cells
key_idea: If a pathogen enters the body, white blood cells destroy it. They engulf pathogens (phagocytosis), make antibodies and make antitoxins. Memory cells remain after infection, so the same pathogen is destroyed faster the next time.

sections.heading: How white blood cells defend the body

blocks.text: If a pathogen gets past the barriers, the immune system tries to destroy it. White blood cells do this in three ways.

items.meaning: A chemical on the surface of a pathogen that the body detects as foreign.
A protein made by white blood cells (lymphocytes) that attaches to an antigen.
A protein that neutralises a toxin made by a pathogen.
A white blood cell (phagocyte) engulfs a pathogen and digests it.

items: **Phagocytosis:** phagocytes engulf pathogens, then digest and kill them.
**Antibodies:** lymphocytes produce antibodies when they detect foreign antigens. Antibodies attach to the pathogen, and may make the cells clump together so phagocytes can engulf more.
**Antitoxins:** these neutralise toxins, so there is less tissue damage and the person does not feel as ill.
Each antibody fits only one antigen, so a different antibody is needed for each pathogen.
Platelets are not white blood cells. They clot the blood and form a scab, which helps to prevent pathogens getting into the body.

blocks.text: How white blood cells are adapted

items: They can change shape to squeeze out of capillaries and reach infected tissue.
Phagocytes make enzymes that digest the pathogens they engulf.
Lymphocytes make antibodies, which are proteins.
All white blood cells have a nucleus. They divide by mitosis after detecting a pathogen.
White blood cells engulf pathogens, produce antibodies and produce antitoxins.
Antibodies are specific to one antigen.

sections.heading: The immune response and memory cells

blocks.text: The first infection by a pathogen is slow to deal with. After it, memory cells make the next response much faster.

diagram.alt: Put the stages of the immune response to a pathogen in order.
diagram.prompt: Put the stages of the immune response in order.
steps: A pathogen with antigens on its surface enters the body
White blood cells detect the foreign antigens
Lymphocytes produce antibodies specific to the antigens
Antibodies attach to the pathogen and help to destroy it
Memory cells are produced and stay in the body
If the pathogen enters again, antibodies are made faster and in larger numbers

items: On the second exposure the correct antibodies are produced sooner, and in greater numbers.
The pathogen is destroyed faster, often before the person feels ill. The person is **immune**.
A person with a damaged immune system, such as in AIDS, cannot kill bacteria as effectively, so they take longer to recover.
Memory cells remain after an infection.
A second infection causes a faster response, with more antibodies.
The person becomes immune to that pathogen.

checks.q: White blood cells help to defend the body against pathogens. How do they do this?
checks.a: They engulf pathogens, produce antibodies and produce antitoxins.
A protein molecule made by the immune system (white blood cells). It destroys pathogens, clumps them together or attaches to antigens.

checks.q: Explain why the immune response is faster the second time a person is infected by the same pathogen.
checks.a: Memory cells (memory lymphocytes) were produced the first time. They produce the correct antibodies faster and in greater numbers.

mistakes.wrong: Phagocytosis helps because white blood cells produce antibodies.
mistakes.right: Phagocytosis is engulfing. Say more pathogens are engulfed and killed by phagocytes, so there is less damage to cells, tissues or organs.
Lymphocytes do not engulf. It is phagocytes that engulf pathogens. Lymphocytes produce antibodies.

mistakes.wrong: A vaccine works because the person is immune.
mistakes.right: Describe both responses. White blood cells produce specific antibodies and memory cells after the vaccine. If the pathogen enters later, the correct antibodies are produced sooner and in greater numbers, so it is destroyed faster.

worked_example.question: White blood cells help to defend the body against pathogens. How do the white blood cells do this?
worked_example.tip: One mark each for three correct ideas. Do not add extra incorrect ideas, as these can cancel marks.

exam_phrases: antigens are on the bacteria, detected by WBCs / phagocytes
antibodies surround / cover / inactivate the antigens / pathogens
memory lymphocytes produce antibodies faster / in greater numbers

mistakes.wrong: The immune system produces antigens to destroy the pathogen.
mistakes.right: "Antigens" is rejected as a way the immune system responds. The pathogen has antigens, and the body responds by producing antibodies.

mistakes.wrong: White blood cells defend the body.
mistakes.right: "WBC" on its own is ignored. Say what they do: lymphocytes produce antibodies, phagocytes engulf pathogens, memory cells give a secondary response.

worked_example.question: Describe how the specific immune system defends the body against disease.
answer_points: These trigger antibodies to be produced.
This leads to the destruction of the pathogen.
These cause a secondary response if there is infection by the same pathogen.
worked_example.tip: Any three linked points score. A secondary response can be described as reacting quickly, before the person gets ill.

exam_phrases: antibodies attach / bind to the antigen
broken down / engulfed by phagocytes / white blood cells

mistakes.right: Do not allow antibodies or lymphocytes engulf. Phagocytes or white blood cells engulf, and white blood cells produce the antibodies.
Do not allow phagocytes produce antibodies. Antibodies are made by white blood cells (lymphocytes).

mistakes.wrong: An antibody attacks or fights germs.
mistakes.right: "Attack", "fight" and "germs" are ignored. An antibody is a protein molecule made by the immune system that destroys pathogens, clumps them together or attaches to antigens.

worked_example.question: Methamphetamine is a drug. Scientists are investigating the use of antibodies as a treatment to control the negative effects of the drug. What is an antibody?
answer_points: Made by the immune system (allow: made by or found in white blood cells).
Destroys or kills pathogens, clumps them together, or attaches to antigens.
worked_example.tip: Any two score. "Germs", "disease", "attack" and "fight" are ignored.
